name: Compressed Biogas (CBG): Blending Mandate & Waste-to-Gas Plant Builders
scope: India's CBG Blending Obligation (CNG/PNG: 1% FY26, 3% FY27, 4% FY28, 5% FY29) is stepping up while blending only just met 1% (PNGRB, Aug-Sep 2026) and only ~210 of ~838 registered plants are commissioned (early Nov 2026), so listed plant builders/operators (small-cap TruAlt Bioenergy, SFC Environmental, Oriana Power; larger DCM Shriram and city-gas utilities) look like the earlier beneficiaries; partly known in retail finance media and the policy is not brand new, but small-cap participants are thinly covered and SFC only listed 3 Nov 2026.
questions: What is the CBG Blending Obligation (CBO): targets by year, who is obligated, penalties, and what changed in the last 1-3 months (FY27 step to 3%, GOBARdhan/Budget support, pipeline connectivity rules)?

How does the CBG value chain work (feedstock such as municipal waste, press mud, napier/agri residue and maize-ethanol by-products; digestion; purification; compression/pipeline injection; fermented organic manure by-product), and what are realistic plant economics (capex per TPD, EBITDA margin, offtake price under SATAT/CBO)?

What is the supply-demand gap: commissioned plants and TPD vs the 838 registered, vs the volume needed to meet 3-5% blending, and how binding is the grid/pipeline connection bottleneck (only ~24 of ~207 functional plants connected per PNGRB)?

What exactly is TruAlt Bioenergy doing in CBG (commissioned 20 TPD Sumitomo JV unit, ~72 TPD target, GAIL JV for ~10 plants, ~Rs 65 cr per plant, GOBARdhan subsidy), and how large is CBG vs its ethanol business in revenue and earnings?

What are SFC Environmental Technologies' CBG plants (reported 125 TPD Tinsukia and 300 TPD Bhubaneswar for a PSU oil marketer, ~Rs 502 cr combined order, and the MGL JV for a 1,000 TPD Deonar plant): verify from the exchange filings/RHP whether it is builder, owner-operator or both, and its order book and margins.

What have Oriana Power (five approved ~22 TPD CBG projects, 110 TPD), DCM Shriram (CBG plant at Ajabpur commissioned Mar 2025), Gujarat Energy/Gujarat Gas (EOI for up to 200 TPD), IGL (CBG plants MoU) and MGL actually disclosed in filings, and which other listed names (e.g. Praj, sugar/ethanol companies, Rajputana Biodiesel) have verifiable CBG plans or capacity?
How do the candidates split across small, mid and large cap, and which have the most CBG exposure relative to their total revenue (pure-play vs line item)? Confirm the correct NSE/BSE symbols.

Has the market already priced this in: 3, 6 and 12-month share-price performance of each candidate, SFC's post-listing move, valuation, and how much mainstream/broker coverage groups these stocks as a CBG theme?

What are the main risks: feedstock cost and availability, offtake price and payment risk, pipeline connection delays, subsidy disbursement delays, execution track record of new entrants, sub-scale plants, low blending compliance so far and penalty enforcement?

What are the upcoming catalysts (Q3 FY27 results, plant commissionings, GAIL/Sumitomo JV progress, subsidy releases, PNGRB compliance data, any CBO target changes or SAF/biogas policy updates) and which stocks are best placed to benefit first?

cbg_plant_developers: Companies building or running compressed biogas plants, including EPC/BOO players, as evidenced by commissioned plants, orders or approved projects
integrated_ethanol_agri: Producers adding CBG to existing ethanol, sugar or chemical sites using by-products and residue as feedstock
gas_utilities_offtake: Obligated CNG/PNG distributors that must meet the blending target and are buying, partnering in or building CBG supply
